items.Sentence: The tertiary wastewater treatment process prior to discharge from Discharge Point 001 includes a bar screen, two aeration basins, four clarifiers, three filters, a tertiary chlorine contact basin, a tertiary effluent clearwell, and four Riverside Ponds that operate in series.
One 5.6-million-gallon Flow Equalization Basin that enables it to collect and store wastewater of any condition from all parts of the treatment plant if needed

After secondary clarification, the Discharger adds sodium hypochlorite and ammonium sulfate to the wastewater (chloramination) to limit the production of trihalomethanes.
wastewater is routed to filters, where polymer is added to improve solids removal
...three filters... After filtration, wastewater is routed to the tertiary chlorine contact basin.
After filtration, wastewater is routed to the tertiary chlorine contact basin.
The Discharger adds sodium bisulfite in the tertiary effluent clearwell prior to routing tertiary-treated wastewater to either the Riverside Ponds or the 20-million-gallon Effluent Storage Pond.
four Riverside Ponds that operate in series... tertiary-treated wastewater is discharged via Discharge Point 001 to the Napa River.
wastewater flow that exceeds the treatment capacity of the filters is routed to the secondary chlorine contact basin, where the Discharger adds sodium hypochlorite for disinfection.
The Discharger adds sodium bisulfite to dechlorinate the wastewater prior to discharge to the Napa River via Discharge Point 002.
Sludge that settles to the bottom of the clarifiers is sent... to a 72,000-gallon-capacity sludge holding tank and then to the sludge drying beds.
A portion of the sludge undergoes anaerobic digestion at the El Nido Composting Facility (Central Valley Composting).
The Discharger hires a contractor to remove the sludge for further treatment or land application (e.g., at the Potrero Hills Landfill or agricultural sites in the Central Valley).
